working_memory.text: The Lindsell seed bank, run from a converted chapel by a group of allotment holders, now holds seed from more than two hundred local varieties of vegetables, including nine kinds of climbing beans grown in the valley for generations. Seed is dried, sealed in foil and stored in a chest freezer, with a second sample kept in a cellar in case the freezer fails. Members grow out each variety every few years to keep the seed fresh. Anyone can borrow seed on the promise of returning some at harvest.
